title: Japan launches mission to bring back a piece of Mars's moon
title_zh: 日本发射探测器，要去火星卫星上挖土带回地球

image.credit: Photo by Behnam Mohsenzadeh on Unsplash
image.author: Behnam Mohsenzadeh

lead: A Japanese-led spacecraft is set to lift off on Monday, aiming to land on Phobos, one of Mars's two small moons, and return a sample to Earth. If successful, it would be the first material ever brought back from Mars or its moons for laboratory analysis.
lead_zh: 由日本牵头的一艘探测器定于周一发射，目标是登陆火星两颗小卫星之一的火卫一，并把样本带回地球。如果成功，这将是人类首次从火星或其卫星带回可供实验室分析的物质。
preview: The Mars Moons Exploration mission, led by the Japanese space agency, is scheduled to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 l
preview_zh: 这项名为“火星卫星探测”的任务由日本宇宙航空研究开发机构牵头，定于当地时间10月20日4时41分从种子岛宇宙中心发射，2027年8月抵达火卫一。内太阳系只有三颗卫星：我们的月球，以及火星的火卫一和火卫二。这两颗火星卫星都很小，形状不规则，看起来就像太空里的土豆。
paragraphs: The Mars Moons Exploration mission, led by the Japanese space agency, is scheduled to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 local time on 20 October, arriving at Phobos in August 2027. There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own, and Phobos and Deimos. Both Martian moons are tiny and irregularly shaped, resembling little more than space potatoes.

Once in the vicinity of Mars, the spacecraft will first study Deimos before turning its attention to Phobos, where it plans to set down a small rover. That will be no mean feat: no rover has ever landed on so small a moon. Phobos has scant gravity of its own, yet sits beside an enormous planet whose pull is far stronger, making any descent considerably harder, according to Sara Russell of the Natural History Museum.

The rover will scout out a landing site so the main spacecraft can later touch down, deploy a robotic arm and two samplers, and collect lunar dust. This will be packed into a small capsule due to return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia. The haul is minuscule — a mere 10 grams — yet scientists insist every gram is worth having.

The sample should finally settle how Mars's moons formed. Either a space rock smashed into the young planet and the debris coalesced into Phobos and Deimos, or the two are wandering asteroids captured by Martian gravity. Russell expects the chemistry and mineral composition to make the answer immediately obvious. There may be a bonus, too: grains of Mars itself could have been implanted in Phobos by impacts.

Bringing Martian material home has long been an ambition. Nasa's Perseverance rover has been caching samples since 2021, but the follow-up Mars Sample Return mission has been effectively cancelled after US Congress halted its funding. China plans its own sampling mission in 2028, aiming to return material in 2031. Martian meteorites do reach Earth, but they are rare and contaminated on arrival; a direct sample would be pristine.
paragraphs_zh: 这项名为“火星卫星探测”的任务由日本宇宙航空研究开发机构牵头，定于当地时间10月20日4时41分从种子岛宇宙中心发射，2027年8月抵达火卫一。内太阳系只有三颗卫星：我们的月球，以及火星的火卫一和火卫二。这两颗火星卫星都很小，形状不规则，看起来就像太空里的土豆。
抵达火星附近后，探测器将先研究火卫二，再把注意力转向火卫一，并计划在那里放下一辆小型巡视车。这绝非易事：此前从未有巡视车登陆过这么小的卫星。据自然历史博物馆的萨拉·拉塞尔介绍，火卫一自身引力微弱，却紧邻一颗引力大得多的巨大行星，这使得任何着陆都难上加难。
巡视车将先勘察着陆点，以便主探测器随后降落，伸出机械臂和两个采样器收集月尘。这些物质将被装入一个小胶囊，预计2031年返回地球，降落在南澳大利亚的伍默拉沙漠。带回的量少得可怜——只有10克——但科学家坚称每一克都值得。
这份样本有望最终解开火星卫星的起源之谜。一种可能是，早期一颗太空岩石撞击火星，碎片聚合成了火卫一和火卫二；另一种可能是，它们是两颗被火星引力俘获的外来小行星。拉塞尔预计，样本的化学成分和矿物组成会让答案一目了然。或许还有意外收获：火星本身的颗粒可能因撞击被嵌入火卫一。
把火星物质带回地球一直是科学家的夙愿。美国航天局的“毅力号”巡视车自2021年起就在采集并封存样本，但后续的“火星样本返回”任务因美国国会停止拨款而实际上已被取消。中国计划在2028年实施自己的采样任务，力争2031年带回火星物质。火星陨石确实会落到地球，但极为罕见，且一落地就已被污染；而直接采集的样本将是纯净的。

vocab.note: 常用于航天报道，比 launch 更生动
描述天体、物体外形的地道搭配
in the vicinity of 表示“在……附近”
固定表达，常用于称赞难度高的事
多修饰抽象名词，如 scant attention
动词短语，含“事先探查”之意
常用于设备、部队、机械臂等
比 small 更强调“微乎其微”
settle a question/mystery 澄清疑问
正式用词，常指碎片、团体合并
天文中指引力俘获天体
此处指颗粒被撞击嵌入卫星表面
航天语境指把样本封存起来备用
强调保持原始状态，未被外界影响
